findings.what: The source scan in worker-provide.test.ts, which is the only check that every engineCall has its provide, has holes. (1) It reads a name only when the name is in single quotes, so engineCall("wythoffEdges", ...) counts as a computed name. (2) For a computed name it only requires that the file provides something; it does not check that the name itself is provided. (3) It does not see engineCall imported under another name. (4) It skips .astro files, so a client <script> there is not scanned for engineCall or for a whole-engine import. (5) Its whole-engine regex misses `export * as X from '@two-games/engine'`. In every one of these cases the test stays green and the call falls back to engineAll the first time someone interacts with the tool. The fallback is silent in production because the warning only exists in development builds.
findings.evidence: Each mutant was applied to the worktree and reverted with git checkout. Then `npx vitest run site/tests/unit/worker-provide.test.ts` gave `Tests 8 passed (8)` for each of: T10 calling engineCall("wythoffEdges", ...) with provide({ orbitGraph }) only; T01 with provide({ raisingPlay }) only (the call name is computed: play, raisingPlay or playFate); a new site/src/lib/zzReviewMutant.ts with `import { engineCall as run }` and run('weylOrder', ...) and no provide; a new ZzReviewMutant.astro whose <script> does `import * as engine from '@two-games/engine'` and engineCall('weylOrder', ...); a new .ts file with `export * as wholeEngine from '@two-games/engine'`. Real effect, shown with the first mutant built to scratch dist-g1: engine-fallback.spec -g geometry gave 3 passed, but the review's ring click on /tools/geometry/?g=A3 logged `A3 ring click: vertexCount 12 -> 24, worker 0, engineAll 1`, a request for http://localhost:7163/_astro/engineAll.kg_rWpDC.js. Controls that the scan does catch: dropping wythoffEdges from T10's provide (1 failed), and the same call split over two lines (1 failed).
findings.specRef: SPEC 7.6 (a tool route carries the engine functions only it uses); CONTRACTS.md 4 provide(); decisions/P6-size.md handoff to T13 and T14
findings.proposedFix: In the scan: read names quoted with ', " or backtick. Treat `engineCall as <alias>` and any reference to engineCall that is not a direct call as calls, or refuse them. Include the <script> blocks of .astro files. Add `export\s+\*\s+as` to the whole-engine regex. For a computed name, require a provide of every string literal the name can take (T01: play and raisingPlay), or an allow-list in the test that names those literals.

findings.what: No browser test watches for an engineAll fetch at an interaction, which is the only moment a fallback can happen today. engine-fallback.spec sweeps default states only, and no default state calls engineCall (the agent's own build that forced every name to fall back still passed). Reading the hints: the only engineCall of a provided engine function that runs on the browser's main thread is T10's orbitGraph and wythoffEdges after a ring or board change. Every other call goes to the worker: T01, T04 orbitGraph with expectedItems 100000, T09 play on, T12 chevalleySerre, and T15 applyWord and firstForbiddenMove (over 2000 moves only). positionsOf and firstForbiddenMove belong to worker.ts. So the one place a missing provide would cost the reader is not watched by any test. T13's satake calls will be the second such place.
findings.evidence: Same G1 build as the first finding: the repo's fallback sweep stayed green (3 passed) while one ring click fetched engineAll. T10.spec itself passes, because the fallback gives correct results.

findings.proposedFix: Add an interaction test to engine-fallback.spec. Watch requests for engineAll and drive one main-thread engineCall per tool that has one: today a ring click on /tools/geometry/?g=A3 that changes vertexCount from 12 to 24, then a draw on E8 1_42 that must reach the worker; later T13's satake on a board below E7. Assert no engineAll request. The scratch review.spec.ts test 3 is a working template.

2 side effects: the top level of all 24 engine modules read with the TypeScript AST. No expression statements. 0 modules register, freeze anything shared, or patch. Engine module ids are plain absolute paths with no query or \0 prefix; a query, a virtual id or a nested path makes the rule return true, the safe default. Returning undefined instead of true for other modules gives byte-identical chunks (293538 B gzip both ways), so 'every other module keeps the default' holds.

notes: Five of the seven provides only matter in Node, because in the browser their hints send the call to the worker: T01 play and raisingPlay, T04 orbitGraph, T09 raisingPlay, T12 chevalleySerre, T15 applyWord. This is harmless, since those modules already ship on their routes for other uses, and it matches the handoff rule.

engine-weight.spec looks for only 3 modules (rep, satake, satakeCatalogue). Its closure starts from astro-island component-url and renderer-url only, so it would not see a page-level <script type=module src> importing the engine. Together with the unscanned .astro files, such an import would only be caught by the size budget.

__testing.reset() does not restore the provided table. Within worker-provide.test.ts the toLabels spy and the stub chevalleySerre stay in the table across tests. Today's order is safe, but test 1's 'not.toContain(chevalleySerre)' depends on running first.

When a fallback does happen, it fetches 8 chunks through __vite__mapDeps (engineAll plus the board, fold, geometry, heaps, rep, weyl and wythoff chunks). That is about 15 kB gzip on /tools/board/. If a deploy replaces the hashed chunks under an open page, the dynamic import fails and the call rejects with a load error instead of an engine error class.
The board chunk also holds svelte/src/version.js and disclose-version.js. This is negligible, and board-load counts that chunk.
